subject: Taxes
title: Wartime Tax and the Social Contract
description: A quick, practical guide to Wartime Tax and the Social Contract.

hook.text: During World War II, the top US tax rate hit 94%. Citizens accepted it willingly.

buildup.text: Before WWII, only 7% of Americans paid income tax. By 1945, 64% did.

discovery.text: Withholding was invented in 1943 to collect taxes in real time. Before this, people paid in lump sums.

twist.text: Post-war, rates stayed high for decades. The top rate didn't drop below 70% until 1982.

climax.text: World War II proved that citizens will accept extraordinary taxes when the cause is clear.

punchline.text: 94% top rate, gladly paid. Shared sacrifice creates tax consent.

quiz.question: What innovation made mass income tax collection possible during WWII?
